Agriculture Cabinet Secretary Mutahi Kagwe noted that national output has grown in recent years, but recent deliveries to formal processors have declined due to diminished pasture and water supplies, prompting government intervention measures.
articles.description: Farmers are receiving higher payments but are producing far less milk and also face rising prices for hay.

articles.headline: Cyclonic storm Akvan forms over Bay of Bengal prompting Andhra Pradesh alerts
articles.title: Cyclonic Storm Akvan forms over the Bay; CM tells officials to take precautionary steps
articles.summary: A deep depression over the Bay of Bengal intensified into Cyclonic Storm Akvan, moving northwest toward the Andhra Pradesh coast and threatening heavy rainfall across several districts. Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu instructed officials to implement precautionary measures and manage floodwaters, while the Fisheries Department issued alerts across twelve coastal districts to ensure returning fishing boats reach safety.
articles.description: The storm may intensify into a Severe Cyclonic Storm by Tuesday evening and may cross the A.P. coast around noon on November 20; rainfall activity may begin in the State from November 18, becoming very heavy on November 19 and 20, according to IMD

articles.headline: Somalia faces political crisis following constitutional overhaul dispute
articles.title: Somalia’s constitutional overhaul tests its fragile federal bargain
articles.summary: President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud dismissed Chief Justice Bashe Yusuf Ahmed a day before the Supreme Court ruled that term extensions could not apply retrospectively. The government rejected the ruling and swore in a replacement, escalating a two-year political conflict over federal power distribution, regional autonomy, and constitutional amendments.
articles.description: Mohamud’s reforms promise stronger government, but regional resistance and violence threaten the fragile deal of 2012.

articles.headline: United States signals no immediate end to ongoing conflict with Iran
articles.title: Is the US-Israel war on Iran turning into a ‘frozen conflict’?
articles.summary: President Donald Trump indicated that the United States is not seeking a new deal with Iran, as the conflict remains unresolved following the collapse of a June truce. With the US maintaining a naval blockade and Iran targeting shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, observers suggest the situation has effectively become a protracted, frozen war.
articles.description: Trump says Washington doesn't need a deal with Tehran, while Iran rejects 'no war, no peace'. Is the war at an impasse?

articles.headline: Trump addresses Quad leaders at first summit since 2024
articles.title: Trump addresses Quad leaders at first summit since 2024
articles.description: US President Donald Trump spoke to leaders of the Quad security bloc at their first summit since 2024.

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coast braces for cyclone Akvan
articles.title: Cyclone Akvan: 540 km of Andhra and Yanam coast braces for November 20 landfall
articles.summary: Cyclonic storm Akvan is moving toward the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coast, with landfall expected around noon on November 20. The India Meteorological Department stated the system will intensify into a severe cyclone. Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu held a review meeting, directing officials to issue warnings and relocate vulnerable pregnant women to safety.
articles.description: Cyclone Akvan is likely to intensify into a very severe cyclonic storm by the evening of November 19 before crossing the Andhra Pradesh coast, the IMD says

articles.headline: U.S. lawmakers introduce eight articles of impeachment against defence secretary
articles.title: What are the eight Articles of impeachment filed against U.S. Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth?
articles.summary: Representative Thomas Massie and supporting lawmakers filed eight articles of impeachment against United States Secretary of Defence Pete Hegseth. The resolution cites alleged violations of the 1973 War Powers Resolution regarding military actions in Iran, civilian casualties from a strike on an Iranian elementary school, maritime strike fatalities, retaliation against Senator Mark Kelly, and the unauthorized capture of former Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro.
articles.description: Representative Thomas Massie, backed by lawmakers including Ro Khanna, has introduced eight Articles of Impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth in the House; here’s what you should know about them

articles.headline: Costa Rican journalist shot dead after reporting on drug trafficking links
articles.title: Gunmen kill Costa Rican journalist who reported on drugs trade
articles.summary: Camilo Rodriguez, a 50-year-old independent journalist, was killed by gunmen on a motorbike near San Jose on Monday. Rodriguez had recently published videos alleging corruption and ties between politicians and drug traffickers. President Laura Fernandez condemned the murder as a threat to free expression, while authorities have launched an investigation into the targeted attack.
articles.description: Rodríguez had denounced alleged links between criminal organisations and powerful figures in Costa Rica.

articles.headline: Israel uses Gaza swimming video to minimise winter hardships
articles.title: Israel uses Gaza swimming video to minimise winter hardships
articles.description: Israel shared an Al Jazeera video of Palestinians swimming, to suggest winter storms in Gaza can’t be that bad.

articles.headline: Why has Waymo pulled all its driverless cars from US freeways?
articles.title: Why has Waymo pulled all its driverless cars from US freeways?
articles.description: The vehicles currently operate in 15 US cities, though freeway rides are only offered in a handful, including San Francisco and Los Angeles.

articles.headline: Migrant boat capsizes off coast of Yenne in Senegal leaving at least one dead
articles.title: Migrant boat capsizes off Senegal, leaving at least one dead
articles.summary: A flat-bottomed pirogue carrying about 100 migrants and refugees struck a rocky area and washed ashore in Yenne, Senegal, resulting in at least one death. A survivor stated the vessel was overcrowded, while local officials noted the area has increasingly become a departure point for smugglers facilitating dangerous maritime journeys toward Europe.
articles.description: Incident comes days after another boat capsized in Senegalese waters, and Spain declared a migration emergency.

articles.headline: US authorities arrest Russian national Igor D'iu for alleged espionage in California
articles.title: Russian arrested for spying on US defence company Palantir over Ukraine support
articles.summary: Federal investigators arrested Igor D'iu, a Russian national accused of acting as a foreign agent to spy on employees at an unnamed technology and defence firm in Palo Alto, California, that assists Ukraine. Prosecutors stated that D'iu entered the United States unlawfully via Mexico in June, stalked workers, and possessed falsified identity documents. Held since November 2, he faces multiple charges carrying over 15 years in prison.
articles.description: The suspect followed employees and was found with fake US IDs and two Russian passports, prosecutors say.

articles.headline: Vessels on fire after naval mine hit in Hormuz Strait, Iran says
articles.title: Vessels on fire after naval mine hit in Hormuz Strait, Iran says
articles.description: Two vessels have caught fire after hitting a naval mine in the Strait of Hormuz.

articles.headline: GTA 6 launches after 13-year wait, breaking pre-order records
articles.title: GTA 6 launches after 13-year wait, breaking pre-order records
articles.description: Grand Theft Auto’s latest instalment is out, ending a 13-year wait for one of gaming’s biggest franchises.

articles.headline: United States investigates Megaspeed over alleged illegal Nvidia chip exports
articles.title: Nvidia partner Megaspeed being investigated by US government over chip exports
articles.summary: The US Department of Justice and Department of Commerce are investigating Singapore-based Megaspeed for potential violations of export controls. Authorities suspect the firm helped divert advanced Nvidia AI chips to China. The probe follows revelations of an affair between Nvidia's former CEO Jensen Huang and Megaspeed's ex-CEO Alice Huang, who is accused of spying for Beijing.
articles.description: The Singapore-based company is suspected of helping to ship high-end AI chips from tech giant Nvidia to China, violating US export rules.

articles.headline: India corporate social responsibility spending leaves funding gaps in health and water security
articles.title: India’s CSR spending leaves gaps in health, water security, innovation: Report
articles.summary: A report by Sattva Consulting and India Data Insights reveals that India's Corporate Social Responsibility funding, which reached ₹40,794 crore in fiscal year 2025, heavily concentrates in education and healthcare while neglecting critical areas like non-communicable diseases, groundwater resilience, and innovation. Co-founder Srikrishna Sridhar Murthy emphasized that corporate spending requires greater agility to address these pressing development challenges effectively.
articles.description: Non-communicable diseases (NCDs), for instance, account for 60% of deaths in India, up from 45% in 2004-06. Yet, nearly 62% of identifiable NCD funding goes towards cancer, while cardiovascular diseases receive around 12%, despite accounting for over half of NCD deaths, says a study by a City-based global impact consulting firm

articles.headline: Iraqi court sentences six French nationals to life for ISIL ties
articles.title: Iraq sentences six French nationals to life in prison for joining ISIL
articles.summary: An Iraqi criminal court sentenced six French nationals to life in prison on Wednesday for joining the ISIL group. The Karkh Criminal Court delivered the sentences with French embassy representatives present, bringing the total number of convicted French citizens in this case to sixteen. Trials began in September for forty-seven French citizens transferred from Syria last year.
articles.description: Trials began in September for 47 French citizens who were transferred from Syria last year.

articles.headline: US lawmakers push legislation to raise federal minimum wage
articles.title: US lawmakers push to raise minimum wage to $25, end tipped pay system
articles.summary: Seventeen United States lawmakers are pushing to pass the Living Wage For All Act to gradually raise the federal minimum wage to twenty-five dollars an hour and eliminate the tipped subminimum wage. The federal rate has remained at seven dollars and twenty-five cents since two thousand and nine, while workers face declining purchasing power and rising living costs.
articles.description: Public support for raising the minimum wage grows, with 78 percent of voters saying it was an important election issue.

articles.headline: Armed robbers loot jewellery worth over thirty crore in Bihar
articles.title: Armed robbers loot jewellery worth more than ₹30 crore at gunpoint in Bihar’s Bettiah
articles.summary: Eight armed robbers looted jewellery valued at more than thirty crore rupees at gunpoint on Wednesday in Bettiah, located in the West Champaran district of Bihar. The daylight heist took place at a Senco Gold and Diamonds showroom owned by Janata Dal United leader Brajesh Kushwaha. Police have formed special teams, reviewed closed-circuit television footage, and launched extensive raids to catch the culprits.
articles.description: According to the police, eight robbers arrived at the jewellery shop on three motorcycles and seized the mobile phone and then tied their hands.

articles.headline: Islam projected to become world's largest religion by 2035
articles.title: Pew Research: Islam on track to become world’s largest religion by 2035
articles.summary: According to the Pew Research Center, Islam is expected to surpass Christianity as the world's largest religion by 2035 due to higher fertility rates of 3.1 children per woman. The global study analysed 201 countries from 2020 to 2070, projecting that Pakistan will overtake Indonesia as the largest Muslim nation while Christian population growth remains concentrated in 120 countries.
articles.description: The report projects steady increases for both Christianity and Islam from 2020 to 2070.

articles.headline: Putin’s nuclear briefcase makes surprise appearance at China summit
articles.title: Putin’s nuclear briefcase makes surprise appearance at China summit
articles.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin’s nuclear briefcase was spotted at the APEC summit in China.

articles.headline: NIA arrests Khalistan Zindabad Force supporter deported from United States
articles.title: NIA arrests Khalistan Zindabad Force ‘supporter’ deported from U.S. in Rajpura-Shambhu blast case
articles.summary: The National Investigation Agency (NIA) arrested Surinder Singh at Delhi airport on November 18, 2026, following his deportation from the United States. Singh is accused of supporting the Khalistan Zindabad Force and glorifying a 2026 railway blast in Punjab. He is the eighth person arrested in connection with the ongoing investigation into the terror conspiracy.
articles.description: Surinder Singh was arrested in connection with the blast on the railway line of the Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Limited (DFCCIL), between Shambhu and Rajpura stations, on April 27

articles.headline: Supreme Court petition questions voter enumeration form numbers in Delhi
articles.title: Plea in Supreme Court asks how many voters have refilled enumeration forms to get back on electoral rolls
articles.summary: Transparency rights activists Anjali Bharadwaj and Amrita Johri filed a petition in the Supreme Court on November 17, 2026, seeking disclosure of Delhi voters who submitted enumeration forms after being deleted from draft electoral rolls under absent, shifted, dead, and duplicate categories. The petitioners requested an extension for submissions, restoration of old EPIC numbers, and an audit of Form 7 applications.
articles.description: Petitioners seek disclosure of the number of ASDD voters who have submitted enumeration forms and want those who used Form 6 to retain their old EPIC numbers

articles.headline: US lawmakers launch probe into Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick
articles.title: US lawmakers launch probe into Lutnick’s actions amid Nvidia scandal
articles.summary: Democratic United States House committee leaders opened an investigation into Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick to determine if his decisions regarding export controls were influenced by holdings of Cantor Fitzgerald, an investment firm controlled by his sons. The probe focuses on whether the firm's financial exposure affected the choice to keep Megaspeed off a trade blacklist.
articles.description: Letter alleges possible conflict of interest in commerce secretary not adding Megaspeed to US trade blacklist.

articles.headline: Karnataka convenes roundtable to operationalize new sustainable data centre policy
articles.title: Karnataka charts 1,000 MW roadmap in consultation with industry stakeholders
articles.summary: Karnataka convened a high-level Data Centre Roundtable in Bengaluru on November 18, 2026, to advance its Sustainable Data Centre Policy 2026-31. Led by Minister Priyank Kharge, the state aims to achieve 1,000 megawatts of cumulative capacity by 2031, decentralizing digital infrastructure to regions like Mangaluru and Mysuru while emphasizing renewable energy and water-efficient cooling technologies.
articles.description: Coastal Karnataka, especially Mangaluru, was highlighted as a strategic growth corridor for capacity expansion and enhanced global connectivity via cable landing stations. The government invites companies to propose concrete interventions for rollout within the next six to twelve months

articles.headline: Madras High Court asked to declare Parandur airport abandonment unconstitutional
articles.title: Declare Parandur airport abandonment decision unconstitutional, insists a PIL plea before Madras High Court
articles.summary: A public interest litigation petition has been filed before the Madras High Court to challenge the Tamil Nadu government's decision to abandon the Parandur greenfield airport project. Software consultant G. Gouthaman argued that Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay illegally used assembly rules on August 24, 2026, to halt the project without technical data, seeking interim stays and file disclosures to protect public investments.
articles.description: Litigant claims the project had been abandoned without any technical data, expert committee report or comparative economic study in support of the decision

articles.headline: Voyager 1 reaches one light-day from Earth after 49 years in space
articles.title: Voyager 1 reaches one light-day from Earth after 49 years in space
articles.description: NASA’s Voyager 1 has reached a record distance of more than 16 billion miles from Earth, 49 years after its launch.

articles.headline: Female students outnumber male admissions in Andhra Pradesh MBBS courses
articles.title: Women outnumber men in admissions to MBBS first year course in Andhra Pradesh
articles.summary: Women accounted for 61.34 percent of admissions to the first-year MBBS course for the 2026–27 academic year in Andhra Pradesh, according to a Health Department release issued on November 18. Authorities submitted seat allotment reports to Health Minister Satya Kumar Yadav, showing that 6,929 of the 6,937 available state quota seats were successfully filled across government and private colleges.
articles.description: Of the total 6,929 seats filled under the State quota, women account for 61.34%, while 38.66% are men; only eight seats remain vacant

articles.headline: TTD plans Vaikunta Dwara Darshan for devotees
articles.title: TTD plans Vaikunta Dwara Darshan for 8.34 lakh devotees this year
articles.summary: The Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams announced plans to facilitate Vaikunta Dwara Darshan for 8.34 lakh devotees at the Lord Venkateswara temple from December 20 to 29. During a meeting on Wednesday, the Specified Authority approved multiple initiatives, including funding for a pilgrim township near Alipiri, environmental protection measures, healthcare expansions, and enhanced financial welfare mechanisms for employees and families of deceased workers.
articles.description: TTD Specified Authority approves selection of a consultancy to prepare the DPR and oversee the proposed ₹2,750-crore pilgrim township near the Alipiri-SV Zoo Park road

articles.headline: TVK cadre social media reels embarrass state government
articles.title: Reels of TVK cadre ‘releasing’ water from Sothuparai Dam embarrass government
articles.summary: Social media videos uploaded by Tamizhaga Vetri Kazhagam cadre claiming to release water from Sothuparai Dam in Theni district prompted an official inquiry on Tuesday. Water Resources Department officials clarified that outsiders only opened a canal sluice rather than the dam itself, utilizing overflow water without authorization. Consequently, the district Collector ordered authorities to lodge a formal police complaint against unidentified individuals.
articles.description: The annual water release ceremony is held only in the presence of elected representatives, the Collector and officials of Water Resources Dept.; after backlash, govt. machinery orders probe

articles.headline: Tamil Nadu government sanctions over six thousand crore rupees for roadworks
articles.title: T.N. government accords administrative sanction of ₹6,513 crore for 2,221 roadworks
articles.summary: The Tamil Nadu government approved six thousand five hundred thirteen point eighteen crore rupees for two thousand two hundred twenty-one road projects under the Comprehensive Road Infrastructure Development Programme for the Highways Department. Public Works Minister Aadhav Arjuna stated the funds will widen congested routes, construct bypasses, and improve safety across state and district roads.
articles.description: They will be executed as part of the Comprehensive Road Infrastructure Development Programme 2026-27

articles.headline: Israeli court extends detention of Gaza hospital director
articles.title: Israeli court extends Gaza doctor Abu Safia’s detention without charge
articles.summary: An Israeli court in Beersheba extended the detention of Hussam Abu Safia, director of Gaza's Kamal Adwan Hospital, for an additional six months without charge. International organizations and the United Nations have previously condemned his prolonged detention and alleged mistreatment, while Israeli authorities claim he poses a threat to the state.
articles.description: An Israeli court extended the detention of Abu Safia nearly two years after Israel's army detained him.

articles.headline: Visakhapatnam civic body prepares control rooms for Cyclone Akvan
articles.title: GVMC gears up for Cyclone Akvan; 11 control rooms, 55 rehabilitation centres readied
articles.summary: The Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation placed its civic machinery on standby and established eleven control rooms to manage potential impacts from approaching Cyclone Akvan. Additional Commissioner S.S. Varma announced that fifty-five rehabilitation centres and numerous rapid response teams were prepared to assist residents in vulnerable low-lying areas.

articles.headline: Disney unveils AI-powered Star Wars Anzellan animatronic prototypes
articles.title: Disney’s new Star Wars animatronics interact with guests using AI
articles.summary: Walt Disney Imagineering R&D has revealed three new Audio-Animatronic prototypes based on Star Wars Anzellan characters, utilizing Amazon Web Services cloud and artificial intelligence capabilities. Equipped with hidden cameras and microphones, the prototypes Vilo Vele, Kado Bre’a, and Jibu Bre’a will debut at the AWS re:Invent conference in Las Vegas to interact with guests using prewritten dialogue and movements.
articles.description: As advanced and lifelike as the animatronic characters at Disney parks have become, they typically either stick to predefined movements and routines, or there's an out of sight puppeteer helping make their behavior appear more spontaneous. That could soon change as Walt Disney Imagineering R&D has revealed three new Audio-Animatronic prototypes that rely on Amazon's […]

articles.headline: Bihar consumer commission penalizes doctor for surgical negligence
articles.title: Bihar doctor fined ₹30 lakh for leaving surgical gauze in abdomen during gallbladder surgery
articles.summary: The Bihar State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission ordered laparoscopic surgeon Rajesh Kumar Singh to pay thirty lakh rupees in compensation to a patient's husband. The penalty follows gross negligence during a gallbladder operation in Saharsa where surgical gauze was left inside fifty-three-year-old Nibha Singh, leading to a fatal infection in July.
articles.description: The Bihar State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission found the doctor guilty of gross medical negligence The case is related to the late Nibha Singh, a resident of Madhepura, Bihar.

articles.headline: Telangana High Court orders transfer of patients from Oasis Fertility
articles.title: HC interim orders over fertility centres
articles.summary: Telangana High Court Justice N.V. Shravan Kumar directed medical officials to transfer fifty-one patients undergoing treatment at Oasis Fertility centres to government IVF facilities. The interim order followed a petition challenging police cases regarding artificial insemination, while a separate hearing was scheduled for doctor Durga Rao.

articles.headline: EPFO faces 1.1 lakh crore financial liability for higher pension claims
articles.title: Higher pension to 4.45 lakh applicants may cost EPFO ₹1.1 lakh crore
articles.summary: Four years following a Supreme Court ruling regarding provident fund pensions based on increased wages, the Employees Provident Fund Organisation stated on November 18, 2026, that implementing the order for over four lakh applicants could cost approximately 1.109 lakh crore rupees. The organisation processed more than 15 lakh applications, issuing demand letters and pension payment orders while addressing ongoing legal challenges and administrative delays.
articles.description: As on November 13, demand letters were issued to 4,45,471 applicants and pension payment orders have been issued to 1,51,874 pensioners

articles.headline: India imposes 162.5% duty and tax on bulk Scotch whisky imports
articles.title: India imposes 162.5% duty and tax on bulk Scotch imports amid UK trade pact dispute
articles.summary: India is enforcing an effective duty and tax of 162.5% on bulk Scotch whisky imports amid a trade agreement dispute with Britain, according to government documents and industry sources. The levy exceeds previous tariffs and has left numerous shipping containers stuck at ports. Importers such as Pernod Ricard and Diageo are arranging bank guarantees to secure their cargo and maintain business operations.
articles.description: More than 80 containers belonging to Pernod Ricard, Diageo and Bacardi remain stuck at Indian ports as the dispute over customs classification threatens to disrupt the liquor industry.

articles.headline: Saudi Arabia prepares for ongoing conflict with Houthi forces into 2027
articles.title: Saudis prepare for Houthi war to last well into 2027
articles.summary: Saudi Arabia is preparing for the conflict with Yemen's Houthis to continue well into next year, aiming for territorial gains by Yemeni allies before engaging in peace talks. According to Western officials, Riyadh expects the campaign to last up to six months following recent battlefield setbacks, while domestic infrastructure faces continued attacks from the group in the ongoing war.
articles.description: Saudi and Yemeni forces are ​now reorganising, with plans to protect Aden from the Houthi advances and potentially shift their offensive to eastern fronts where they have made some advances or have at least held their lines

articles.headline: ACME Group finalizes 3.6 billion dollar green ammonia project in Odisha
articles.title: ACME seals $3.6-billion deal for Odisha green ammonia project
articles.summary: ACME Group has completed formalities for a 3.6 billion dollar green ammonia facility in Paradip, Odisha, with a 600 million dollar investment from Brookfield. Expected to be commissioned by 2029, the plant will produce 760,000 tonnes annually using renewable energy. The project aims to supply green molecules to both domestic fertiliser companies and international markets.
articles.description: With an annual production capacity of 760,000 tonnes, the facility is expected to be commissioned by 2029.

articles.headline: New video shows explosions moments before part of Crimea Bridge collapses
articles.title: New video shows explosions moments before part of Crimea Bridge collapses
articles.description: BBC Verify analyses footage showing the final moments before part of the bridge fell and videos showing the scale of destruction.

articles.headline: Security forces engage in fresh encounter with terrorists in Jammu and Kashmir's Kulgam district
articles.title: LeT’s ‘last local recruit’ Lateef Bhat killed outside a Kulgam mosque
articles.summary: Security forces and terrorists engaged in a renewed firefight in the Kulgam district of Jammu and Kashmir on November 18, 2026. The operation followed an ongoing search for Lateef Bhat, a wanted Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorist who escaped a previous cordon that resulted in the killing of associate Umar Nisar Dar.
articles.description: Bhat, who was behind the attack on a CRPF checkpost last month, was hiding in the mosque and turned down an offer to surrender, security forces say; Home Minister Amit Shah praises synergy of forces in operation

articles.headline: Bombay High Court quashes prosecution sanction against former ICICI Bank CEO
articles.title: Bombay HC sets aside ICICI Bank Board of Directors’ sanction order on Chanda Kochhar
articles.summary: The Bombay High Court quashed ICICI Bank's sanction to prosecute former chief executive officer Chanda Kochhar regarding alleged irregularities in a loan issued to the Videocon Group in 2012. Justice Milind Jadhav ruled that the issuing authority failed to apply its mind and lacked competence. The Central Bureau of Investigation had previously alleged a quid pro quo involving a ₹3,250-crore loan and investments in a company belonging to Kochhar's husband.
articles.description: The court held that the Reserve Bank of India constitutes the authority with jurisdiction under Section 36-AA(1) of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 to grant permission

articles.headline: Ukrainian forces fight Russian troops inside an underground gas pipeline in Kharkiv
articles.title: Inside the old gas pipeline where Ukraine is fighting an underground war with Russia
articles.summary: Ukrainian forces have spent seven months fighting Russian troops inside a Soviet-era gas pipeline in the Kharkiv region. The British Broadcasting Corporation reported on the subterranean operations near Kupyansk, where narrow conditions provide shelter from aerial drones that currently prevent troops from advancing on the surface.
articles.description: Watch: The BBC's Jonathan Beale joins Ukrainian forces taking the battle below ground and out of sight of Russian drones.

articles.headline: Ukrainian troops use subterranean Soviet gas pipeline to fight Russian forces in Kharkiv
articles.title: 'The drones don't fly here' - BBC reports from Ukraine's new front line
articles.summary: Ukrainian forces have spent seven months fighting Russian troops inside a Soviet-era gas pipeline in the Kharkiv region to bypass aerial drones. Operating as part of the 13th Khartiia Brigade of Ukraine's National Guard, soldiers have advanced 15 kilometers along the tunnel network since April in an underground operation involving domestic troops and foreign volunteers.
articles.description: Ukrainian forces are fighting Russian troops in an old Soviet tunnel in the Kharkiv region.

articles.headline: IAEA chief Rafael Grossi welcomes United States and Saudi Arabia nuclear agreement
articles.title: U.S.-Saudi nuclear agreement 'satisfactory': IAEA
articles.summary: International Atomic Energy Agency head Rafael Grossi expressed satisfaction on Wednesday with a bilateral agreement between the United States and Saudi Arabia concerning a civilian nuclear program. Grossi told reporters that both nations requested verification measures in October, granting the agency access to conversion, enrichment, and fuel fabrication sites across Saudi Arabia.
articles.description: According to the accord, the IAEA "will be provided with information about, and access to any sites for conversion, enrichment, fuel fabrication and reprocessing" in Saudi Arabia, Grossi said

articles.headline: Army officer dies after vehicle plunges into river in Manipur
articles.title: Captain dies after Army vehicle plunges into Itam River in Imphal East
articles.summary: An Army officer died and three soldiers were injured after their military vehicle fell into the Itam River in Imphal East, Manipur, on November 18, 2026. Captain Hanuman Ram, 29, died at a hospital, while three others remain in serious condition. The circumstances surrounding the accident in the Lamlai Challou area remain currently unclear.
articles.description: Three soldiers were injured when a military vehicle carrying troops of the 8th Bihar Regiment fell into the river

articles.headline: World Bank says Lebanon reconstruction progress is slow
articles.title: World Bank official says Lebanon reconstruction making slow progress
articles.summary: World Bank managing director of operations Anna Bjerde stated that Lebanon has been slow to utilise international aid for rebuilding areas destroyed during conflicts. An approved 250 million dollar loan faced parliamentary delays and ongoing Israeli military occupation, while the United Nations estimates that over 300,000 Lebanese remain internally displaced across the country.
articles.description: Beirut blames Israel's occupation and attacks on southern Lebanon for reconstruction delays.

articles.headline: Megha Engineering and Infrastructures raises 700 million dollars from global investors
articles.title: MEIL Group raises $700 million from global investors at ₹1 lakh crore valuation
articles.summary: Megha Engineering and Infrastructures Ltd. (MEIL) Group has secured approximately 700 million dollars from three global investment firms, including Värde Partners, at a valuation of 1 lakh crore rupees. The capital raise supports the group's diverse infrastructure portfolio, which spans irrigation, energy, and transportation projects across 20 countries, including major developments like the Zojila Tunnel.
articles.description: MEIL has expanded its footprint to more than 20 countries, building a diversified portfolio spanning irrigation, transportation, energy, oil and gas, manufacturing, clean mobility and advanced infrastructure.

articles.headline: Singer Julio Iglesias faces Spanish court investigation over sexual assault allegations
articles.title: Julio Iglesias facing court investigation over alleged sexual offences
articles.summary: Spanish national court Judge Antonio Piña announced on Wednesday that criminal proceedings have been opened against 83-year-old singer Julio Iglesias regarding allegations of sexual abuse and assault involving two former staff members in the Bahamas and the Dominican Republic in 2021. The complainants have been summoned to testify in person on February 3, following a previous dismissal of the case by prosecutors who later shifted their jurisdictional stance.
articles.description: The 83-year-old singer is accused of abusing two former employees at Caribbean residences in 2021.

articles.headline: Government amends Export Promotion Mission guidelines to support small exporters
articles.title: Govt relaxes guidelines under Export Promotion Mission to help MSME exporters reach new markets
articles.summary: The Ministry of Commerce and Industry has amended Export Promotion Mission guidelines to help micro, small and medium enterprises reach new markets. Changes include increased airfare reimbursement, expanded certification support for international standards, and wider logistics coverage for low-intensity districts. These updates aim to address logistical gaps and empower exporters under the Niryat Disha sub-scheme.
articles.description: So far, a total of 11 interventions under two sub-schemes of the Export Promotion Mission have been operationalised

articles.headline: Jerusalem Daily: Chaos in the Knesset as new speaker elected
articles.title: Jerusalem Daily: Chaos in the Knesset as new speaker elected
articles.description: Israel’s army beat a journalist covering a settler attack near Jericho.

articles.headline: Tata Steel partners with Utility Global for hydrogen production project in Odisha
articles.title: Tata Steel plans hydrogen production using steel plant off-gases
articles.summary: Tata Steel has announced a collaboration with Houston-based Utility Global to launch India's first plant producing high-purity hydrogen from steel plant off-gases at Kalinganagar in Odisha. Scheduled for November 18, 2026, the ten-tonne-per-day facility uses H2Gen technology to reduce emissions. According to Tata Steel, the initiative supports the company's commitment to achieving net zero carbon emissions by 2045 through sustainable operational decarbonisation.

articles.headline: French court sentences parents for torture and death of four-year-old girl
articles.title: Parents jailed for torture and death of four-year-old girl found along French motorway in 1987
articles.summary: A court in central France sentenced 72-year-old Halima El Bakhti to twenty years in prison on Tuesday for acts of torture resulting in death without intent, while the victim's father, 74-year-old Ahmed Touloub, received a fifteen-year sentence as an accomplice. The four-year-old girl, known for decades as the Little Martyr of the A10, was discovered dead along a motorway on August 11, 1987, and was finally identified in 2018 through familial DNA testing.
articles.description: Inass Touloub's body was found along the A10 road in 1987, bearing marks of abuse, and was not identified until 2018.

articles.headline: Cameron Bancroft asserts entire team knew about 2018 ball-tampering conspiracy
articles.title: ‘It was the whole team’: Bancroft opens up on Sandpapergate
articles.summary: Cameron Bancroft asserted that the entire Australian team knew about the 2018 ball-tampering conspiracy in South Africa, stating he took the burden for everyone. Bancroft supported recent claims by former batter Usman Khawaja after captain Pat Cummins dismissed them. Cricket Australia announced it will study Bancroft's statement and establish a forum for individuals to provide their version of events.
articles.description: Cameron Bancroft says the entire Australian team knew of the 2018 ball-tampering plan, backing Usman Khawaja’s claim, as Cricket Australia says it will study his comments

articles.headline: India targets illegal cannabis and opium cultivation in nationwide operations
articles.title: India’s drug crackdown: illegal cannabis and opium cultivation targeted in NCB-led operations
articles.summary: The Narcotics Control Bureau conducted nationwide operations alongside state police and security forces to eliminate illicit cannabis and opium cultivation. The crackdown spans multiple states including Tripura, Rajasthan, and Himachal Pradesh, aligning with the Union Home Ministry goal to eradicate poppy and cannabis farming by December 2027 through coordinated destruction drives.
articles.description: Operations across Tripura, Himachal Pradesh, Arunachal Pradesh, Rajasthan and Jharkhand cover forest land, remote hill districts, and community lands

articles.headline: How are we able to record sounds? How do they sound like what we hear in real life?
articles.title: How are we able to record sounds? How do they sound like what we hear in real life?

articles.headline: Enforcement Directorate summons associates in CMRL-Exalogic pay-off scam probe
articles.title: ED summons Riyas’s associates as part of probe into alleged CMRL-Exalogic pay-off scam
articles.summary: The Directorate of Enforcement issued notices to associates of former Public Works department minister P.A. Mohamed Riyas in the ongoing investigation into the Cochin Minerals and Rutile Limited and Exalogic Solutions pay-off scam. The probe was revived after the Kerala High Court dismissed a plea to quash the case, following earlier raids that froze multiple bank accounts and records.
articles.description: The summons have been issued in connection with the first ECIR (Enforcement Case Information Report) registered in 2024. Reportedly, the ED is planning to file the first chargesheet in the case shortly

articles.headline: Eight workers rescued from long-term bonded labour in Narayanpet
articles.title: Eight workers, including 16-year-old boy, rescued from bonded labour in Narayanpet
articles.summary: Revenue, labour, and police officials rescued eight workers from bonded labour at a construction site in Narayanpet town after they suffered years of debt bondage. The group, including minors and elderly individuals, was denied proper wages and freedom of movement before seeking help through a government toll-free helpline campaign.
articles.description: The group included an elderly couple from Wanaparthy, aged 78 and 66, and a young couple from Mahbubnagar, aged 19 and 22. Seven of the eight workers belong to the Scheduled Caste community.

articles.headline: Pan-Indian study links higher DNA fragment levels to stronger cancer blood signals
articles.title: Pan-Indian study finds that higher levels of DNA fragments in blood strengthen cancer signals
articles.summary: A four-year study across forty-three Indian hospitals evaluated the CancerSpot blood test, finding it detected seventy-two percent of cancer cases across fourteen types with a low false-positive rate. Developed by Strand Life Sciences, the test combines DNA sequencing and artificial intelligence to analyse circulating cell-free DNA methylation patterns in patients.
articles.description: CancerSpot test records 72% detection rate and 1.4% false positives; the test aims to detect multiple types of cancer through a single blood test, without requiring a tissue biopsy for the initial detection

articles.headline: Ukrainian military launches precision drone and missile attacks on Crimean bridge
articles.title: ‘Crimea is turning into an island’: How Ukraine hit Putin’s prized bridge
articles.summary: The Ukrainian military launched precision drone and cruise missile attacks on Tuesday against the bridge linking southern Russia to Crimea, collapsing an arch and damaging tarmac. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy called the operation flawless, while the Kremlin accused Kyiv of escalating the war and vowed to restore the crossing. Observers noted the destruction disrupts transport routes as Russia simultaneously strikes bridges across Ukraine.
articles.description: A weeks-long operation was behind two waves of strikes using long-range missiles and drones developed in Ukraine.

articles.headline: US and Iran maintain limited confrontation amid economic and political strain
articles.title: Can the US and Iran sustain a ‘frozen war’?
articles.summary: The United States and Iran have settled into a pattern of limited military engagement following the collapse of a June memorandum. Both nations continue to trade attacks and enforce naval blockades, particularly around the Strait of Hormuz. Analysts warn that while this status quo avoids all-out war, it imposes significant economic costs on both sides.
articles.description: Tehran may eventually decide that 'escalating confrontation' is preferable to status quo, says analyst Hamidreza Azizi.

articles.headline: What’s holding South Africa’s economy back?
articles.title: What’s holding South Africa’s economy back?
articles.description: South Africa seeks billions in new investment to revive weak growth and tackle unemployment crisis.

articles.headline: Mada Masr’s Lina Attalah due to appear before court in Egypt
articles.title: Mada Masr’s Lina Attalah due to appear before court in Egypt
articles.description: Mada Masr Editor-in-Chief Lina Attalah is set to face a retrial before an Egyptian criminal court.

articles.headline: Israel continues military incursions in southern Syria despite political transition
articles.title: What is the ‘endgame’ in Syria, as Israeli rivals look for new government?
articles.summary: Israeli forces have intensified raids and ground incursions in southern Syria, occupying strategic areas including Mount Hermon since December 2024. Despite upcoming changes to Israel's government, experts suggest security policies will remain unchanged. The Syrian government, led by President Ahmed al-Sharaa, faces ongoing instability as Israeli military actions continue to disrupt local governance and security.
articles.description: As Israel intensifies its incursions into southern Syria, analysts say there will be little change in the future.

articles.headline: House Democrats prepare to nominate Hakeem Jeffries for speaker
articles.title: How the US House of Representatives chooses its leaders: A visual guide
articles.summary: House Democrats are set to vote on Wednesday to nominate Hakeem Jeffries for speaker of the United States House of Representatives. Following their victory in the November 3 midterm elections, Democrats hold a majority of seats. If confirmed in the full House vote on January 3, Jeffries would become the first Black speaker in American history.
articles.description: After their midterm win, Democrats will lead the House from January 3. Here’s how its speaker and leaders are chosen.

articles.headline: Stock markets decline as Sensex drops 500 points amid profit booking
articles.title: Stock markets snap 2-day rally; Sensex drops 500 points amid profit booking, U.S. Fed rate hike fears
articles.summary: Benchmark equity indices ended lower on Wednesday, snapping a two-day rally as the BSE Sensex fell 500.38 points to settle at 82,031.81 while the NSE Nifty declined 159.45 points to 25,227.95. According to market analysts, the downturn was driven by profit booking in consumer durables and metal shares, alongside rising domestic yields and hawkish remarks from United States Federal Reserve officials regarding potential rate hikes.
articles.description: 30-share BSE Sensex drops 500.38 points, or 0.61%, to settle at 82,031.81; 50-share NSE Nifty declines 159.45 points, or 0.63%, to end at 25,227.95

articles.headline: Supreme Court dismisses plea seeking ban on ritual animal sacrifices
articles.title: SC dismisses plea against animal killing during religious ceremonies
articles.summary: The Supreme Court dismissed a petition seeking to prohibit animal killings during religious ceremonies and temple rituals across India. A Bench comprising Justices Vikram Nath, R. Mahadevan and Aparesh Kumar Singh rejected the plea filed by advocate Shruti Bisht, which challenged statutory exemptions under the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act of 1960. The petitioner had argued that the practice violated the right to life guaranteed under Article 21 of the Constitution.
articles.description: A Bench of Justices Vikram Nath, R. Mahadevan and Aparesh Kumar Singh dismissed advocate Shruti Bisht’s plea to amend the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960

articles.headline: Supreme Court issues notice on contempt plea against lawyer Pravin Singhal
articles.title: Supreme Court issues notice on contempt plea against lawyer over remarks about CJI
articles.summary: The Supreme Court issued notice on a petition by the Supreme Court Bar Association seeking criminal contempt proceedings against advocate Pravin Singhal for alleged disparaging remarks about Chief Justice of India Surya Kant. A Bench led by Justice Dipankar Datta noted a prima facie case existed, supported by the Attorney General for India's consent. The court instructed the respondent to respond by January 8 and appear personally on January 20.
articles.description: Solicitor General Tushar Mehta supported the Supreme Court Bar Association’s petition, submitting that ‘the majesty of the court cannot be compromised’

articles.headline: Mathematician Riddhipratim Basu wins 2026 Infosys Prize
articles.title: Keep humans at centre of math as we adapt to AI: Infosys laureate
articles.summary: Mathematician Riddhipratim Basu has been awarded the 2026 Infosys Prize in the mathematical sciences category. Dr. Basu serves as an associate professor at the International Centre for Theoretical Sciences, Bengaluru, part of the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research. His academic research focuses on utilizing mathematical frameworks to understand how random events generate predictable patterns across physical systems.
articles.description: Riddhipratim Basu has been awarded the 2026 Infosys Prize in mathematical sciences. In his work, he uses mathematics to understand how random events produce predictable patterns in physical systems

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh faces threat of third cyclone in a month
articles.title: Cyclone Akvan: why is Andhra Pradesh facing a third cyclone in a month?
articles.summary: Coastal districts in Andhra Pradesh face an imminent threat from cyclonic storm Akvan, which follows severe cyclonic storms Arnab on October 28 and Murasu on November 3. Experts attribute this rare post-monsoon triple-storm scenario to super El Niño conditions, high sea surface temperatures exceeding 26.5 degrees Celsius in the Bay of Bengal, and barrier layers created by massive freshwater discharge from major rivers.
articles.description: Warm seas, river water that traps heat near the surface and winds that steer storms towards the coast have made this post-monsoon season unusual, experts say

articles.headline: Security forces rescue twenty-seven civilians during Kulgam counter-terrorism operation
articles.title: Kulgam encounter: 25 girls, 2 teachers rescued before final assault on LeT commander Bhat
articles.summary: Troops from the 9 Rashtriya Rifles and the Jammu and Kashmir Police successfully evacuated 25 girls and two teachers from a seminary in Kulgam district on Wednesday before launching a final assault against Lashkar-e-Taiba commander Mohammad Lateef Bhat. The operation concluded after intelligence inputs located Bhat inside the mosque, where he was neutralised following extensive cordon and search operations deployed across the region.
articles.description: Once the civilians were moved to safety, security forces launched the final onslaught.

articles.headline: Piyush Goyal meets Italian corporate leaders in Rome to expand investments
articles.title: Union Minister Piyush Goyal meets top Italian CEOs in Rome to boost investment, tech partnerships
articles.summary: Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Piyush Goyal held discussions with chief executive officers of leading Italian firms in Rome on Tuesday to boost bilateral trade toward a target of €20 billion by 2029. The meetings focused on joint ventures and technology transfers across manufacturing, aerospace, and healthcare sectors, reinforcing Italy's status as India's fourth-largest trading partner within the European Union.
articles.description: Mr. Goyal met chief executives and senior leaders of Italian companies on November 17, as India and Italy work towards a target of €20 billion in annual bilateral trade by 2029

articles.headline: How data centres are turning AI-generated heat into energy
articles.title: How data centres are turning AI-generated heat into energy
articles.description: How data centres are turning AI-generated heat into energy

articles.headline: Ukraine mourns mother, athlete and drone operator killed in Russian strike
articles.title: Ukraine mourns mother, athlete and drone operator killed in Russian strike
articles.description: Rayana joined Ukraine’s army in 2024 to protect her son from Russia’s invasion. She was killed in Russian air strike.

articles.headline: Disagreements stall implementation of Washington accords between Rwanda and DRC
articles.title: Rwanda and DRC: What is holding up the Washington peace process?
articles.summary: Negotiations between the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Rwanda continue to face obstacles regarding the implementation of the Washington Accords for Peace and Prosperity. Disagreements center on defining compliance for neutralising the Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Rwanda and lifting Rwandan defensive measures, further complicated by recent United States sanctions against the Rwandan Ministry of Defence.
articles.description: The two sides remain divided over key security commitments under the Washington Accords.

articles.headline: BRS leader K.T. Rama Rao accuses Telangana government of aiding Andhra Pradesh water diversion
articles.title: KTR accuses Telangana government of aiding Andhra Pradesh in Krishna water diversion attempts
articles.summary: Bharat Rashtra Samithi working president K.T. Rama Rao accused the Congress government in Telangana of facilitating Andhra Pradesh in diverting Krishna waters through an unauthorised scheme. Speaking in Hyderabad on Wednesday, he alleged that Andhra Pradesh had been excavating a tunnel near Vijayapuri South for nearly a year. He demanded intervention from the Krishna River Management Board and warned of potential legal action and agitations.
articles.description: BRS working president claims that Andhra Pradesh was using a drinking water scheme as a pretext to develop a 1,650-km pipeline network to divert nearly nine tmcft of water, threatening Telangana’s irrigation and drinking water interests

articles.headline: Kerala University researchers secure Indian patent for advanced solar-active hydrogen production material
articles.title: Kerala University research team secures patent for solar-active hydrogen production material
articles.summary: A research team from Kerala University received an Indian patent for developing a cobalt-doped zinc ferrite nanostructure designed for photocatalytic hydrogen generation. The material absorbs solar radiation from the ultraviolet to near-infrared region using an ultralow concentration of cobalt. Researchers achieved a hydrogen production rate of 439.8 mmol per hour and an apparent quantum efficiency of 88.7% under experimental conditions.
articles.description: The development of efficient photocatalysts capable of utilising a wider portion of the solar spectrum is key to the transition towards sustainable and environmentalfriendly energy technologies.

articles.headline: DMK president M.K. Stalin declines phone call from Congress leader Rahul Gandhi
articles.title: DMK leader Stalin avoids Rahul Gandhi’s phone call, greets Sonia on her memoir
articles.summary: DMK president M.K. Stalin avoided a call from Congress leader Rahul Gandhi regarding an invitation to Sonia Gandhi's book launch in New Delhi. Sources indicate the relationship between the two leaders has strained since the Congress party joined the TVK-led government six months ago. Stalin sent a congratulatory message for the book release instead of speaking.
articles.description: Sources say DMK chief didn’t wish to engage with Congress leader following strains in their ‘brotherly’ bond in the run-up to the last Assembly election and the Congress jumping ship after the results

articles.headline: CBIC prepares draft framework for faceless and centralised assessment of CGST taxpayers
articles.title: To soon issue draft framework for centralised assessment of CGST taxpayers: CBIC chief
articles.summary: The Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs announced on November 18, 2026, that a draft framework for faceless and centralised assessment for 70 lakh Central Goods and Services Tax taxpayers will soon be released for public consultation. Chairman Vivek Chaturvedi stated that the system, targeting implementation from April 1, 2027, aims to streamline administration for large enterprises and small entrepreneurs alike across India.
articles.description: The new framework is likely to be implemented from next fiscal beginning April 1, 2027

articles.headline: India Meteorological Department withdraws heavy rain alert for four districts in Telangana
articles.title: Cyclone Akvan forecast track changes, heavy rain alert withdrawn for Telangana’s four districts
articles.summary: The India Meteorological Department withdrew its heavy to very heavy rainfall forecast for Bhadradri Kothagudem, Khammam, Suryapet and Mahabubabad districts on Wednesday as cyclonic storm Akvan is expected to weaken. According to the updated forecast, the cyclone is likely to cross the north Andhra Pradesh, Yanam and south Odisha coasts on Friday. Only thunderstorms with lightning are now predicted for several districts in Telangana.

articles.headline: Indian Space Research Organisation candidate selection process for human spaceflight missions
articles.title: How did ISRO pick astronaut candidates for the Gaganyaan mission?
articles.summary: National space agencies historically select military test pilots as initial spacefarers because they possess advanced technical skills and rigorous emergency training. According to the published report on November 19, 2026, civilian specialists including scientists and engineers are typically integrated into crewed missions only after launch systems are fully matured through uncrewed test flights.
articles.description: As India embarks on its first manned space mission, developing indigenous capabilities in crew selection and training not only lays the foundation for sustained space activities but also gives an impetus to bioastronautics — the study of behavioural, and medical aspects of humans living in space

articles.headline: Tata Electronics flags supply chain and talent gaps in major semiconductor manufacturing push
articles.title: Tata Electronics flags supply chain, talent gaps in ₹1.18 lakh crore semiconductor push
articles.summary: Tata Electronics is addressing critical supply chain constraints, logistics hurdles and talent gaps as it invests up to ₹1.18 lakh crore in semiconductor facilities in Gujarat and Assam. Speaking on Tuesday, Srinivas Satya noted challenges in building a domestic supplier ecosystem and moving specialised equipment. The company is establishing a fabrication plant in Dholera and an outsourced assembly and test facility in Jagiroad.
articles.description: Tata Electronics is currently engaging with 1,200-1,300 suppliers across its electronics and semiconductor businesses, with more than 500 involved in construction alone.

articles.headline: Historical notes reveal origins of famous scientific image of molecular structure
articles.title: Rosalind Franklin’s notes crack mystery of DNA’s most famous photo
articles.summary: Rosalind Franklin and doctoral student Raymond Gosling captured the clearest experimental X-ray image of the B form of deoxyribonucleic acid on May 2, 1952. Labelled Photograph 51, the historic scientific image later inspired a British commemorative coin issued in 2020 to mark the birth centenary of the pioneering researcher.
articles.description: Photograph 51 is one of the most iconic images in the history of science, featuring in several lists of the most important photographs ever taken. Its fame comes not only from the role it played in revealing DNA’s helical structure but also from the controversy surrounding its use and the subsequent debate on credit

articles.headline: Displaced Palestinian families seek refuge in ancient caves after Israeli army demolitions
articles.title: Palestinians find refuge in ancient caves after Israel demolishes homes
articles.summary: Residents of Khallet al-Daba in the occupied West Bank have sought shelter in ancient caves after the Israeli army demolished their homes multiple times. According to locals and United Nations reports, decades of demolitions and the expansion of illegal outposts have forced dozens of families to live in damp, poorly ventilated underground spaces amid rising settler attacks and severe restrictions on water and electricity.
articles.description: Palestinians displaced in the occupied West Bank's Masafer Yatta area have been forced to live in underground caves.

articles.headline: European governments plan deportation centre in Rwanda for rejected asylum seekers
articles.title: ‘Partnership buys silence’: Fears grow over EU-Rwanda deportation plans
articles.summary: Germany, Denmark, Greece, Austria and the Netherlands announced plans on Monday to establish a deportation centre in Rwanda for rejected asylum seekers. Human rights organisations have criticised the proposal, citing concerns over Rwanda's human rights record and freedom of expression. Rwandan Interior Minister Vincent Biruta defended the country's record, stating that human rights are respected for everyone.
articles.description: A British immigration lawyer, Rwandan journalist, rights groups and leading politicians decry the proposal as inhumane.

articles.headline: Saudi-led coalition strikes Houthi military sites in Yemen following advance
articles.title: Saudi coalition hits 60 Houthi military sites; Taiz sees ‘fierce battles’
articles.summary: Saudi-led coalition forces conducted precision airstrikes against 60 Houthi military targets in Yemen on Tuesday, destroying tunnels and ballistic missile workshops. According to coalition spokesman Turki al-Maliki, the strikes occurred during a Houthi advance towards Aden. Meanwhile, local authorities in Taiz accused the Houthi group of blocking medical supplies and shelling residential neighbourhoods, endangering civilian lives.
articles.description: Houthis advance towards Aden as Saudi-led coalition conducts precision strikes on key military targets in Yemen.

articles.headline: India-U.S. trade deal signing will take time due to U.S. tariff reviews
articles.title: India-U.S. trade deal signing will still ‘take some time’, says Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal
articles.summary: Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal stated on November 18, 2026, that the formal signing of the India-U.S. trade agreement will be delayed while the United States finalises its new tariff architecture and concludes Section 301 investigations. While negotiations and the legal text are nearly complete, Agrawal noted that ongoing investigations regarding forced labour and excess capacity create uncertainty that must be resolved first.
articles.description: He added that the deal can be signed only after the U.S. finalises its new tariff framework. Recently, Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal said the two nations had agreed that India would receive an advantage over its competitors

articles.headline: Who would gain from carving up Pakistan’s provinces?
articles.title: Who would gain from carving up Pakistan’s provinces?
articles.description: Pakistan could split four provinces into 12, raising hopes of better governance and fears of greater military power.

articles.headline: Goldman Sachs predicts Reserve Bank of India will raise interest rates
articles.title: RBI may hike interest rates by 75 basis points by Q2 CY27: Goldman Sachs
articles.summary: Goldman Sachs Research projected that the Reserve Bank of India may increase the benchmark repo rate by 75 basis points by the second quarter of calendar year 2027 to address rising food prices and inflationary pressures. According to Chief India Economist Santanu Sengupta, inflation has exceeded the central bank target, reaching 6.1 percent in October, prompting expectations of continued monetary tightening.
articles.description: The interest rate hike is expected to moderate India's real GDP growth to 7.2% in CY27, down from an estimated 7.9% in CY26

articles.headline: NASA probe Voyager 1 reaches one light-day distance milestone
articles.title: NASA Voyager 1 probe believed to have reached ‘light-day’ milestone
articles.summary: NASA calculated that the robotic probe Voyager 1 reached a distance of one light-day from Earth on November 18, 2026, traveling at roughly 38,000 miles per hour through interstellar space. Launched in 1977, the spacecraft continues gathering scientific measurements of magnetic fields and cosmic rays using remaining instrument power expected to last through next year.
articles.description: The robotic probe, launched in 1977, was calculated by NASA to have reached a light-day from Earth, ‌the distance that light travels in 24 hours — about 26 billion km

articles.headline: India targets one trillion dollars in exports for the fiscal year
articles.title: India on track to hit $1 trillion exports this year: Commerce Secretary
articles.summary: Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal announced on November 18, 2026, that India is on track to achieve one trillion dollars in goods and services exports for the 2026-27 fiscal year. Speaking at an event hosted by the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry, Agrawal noted that exports grew by 16.6 percent during the April-September period, building on the record 863 billion dollars reached last fiscal.
articles.description: Last fiscal, India had touched an all-time high of $863 billion

articles.headline: China supercomputer LineShine retains top spot on global list
articles.title: China’s LineShine retains top spot on list of world’s most powerful supercomputers
articles.summary: China’s LineShine supercomputer retained its number one position on the Top500 list at the SC26 conference in Chicago on November 16, 2026. Built by the Shenzhen Cloud Computing Centre for atmospheric and ocean research, the system performed 2.198 quintillion calculations per second during testing. This achievement highlights domestic technological advancement despite United States chip restrictions.
articles.description: The highest ranked Indian machine on the list is Shakti Cloud at number 35

articles.headline: Cameron Bancroft claims entire Australian cricket team knew of 2018 plot
articles.title: Bancroft sandpaper claims heap pressure on Cummins
articles.summary: Batter Cameron Bancroft released detailed testimony claiming the entire Australian playing group and staff knew about the 2018 ball-tampering plot against South Africa. Published ahead of a Cricket Australia forum, the revelations challenge previous denials by captain Pat Cummins and coach Darren Lehmann, heightening pressure on team leadership before the upcoming Test match against New Zealand on December 9.
articles.description: Cameron Bancroft claims the whole Australia team knew about the 2018 sandpaper plot in explosive revelations that will heap pressure on current captain Pat Cummins.

articles.headline: Liquefied petroleum gas tanker sank off Bulgarian coast after strikes
articles.title: LPG tanker that sank off Bulgaria was hit by projectiles: official
articles.summary: The Liberian-flagged Gas Husky sank off Byala on November 17, 2026, after sustaining four projectile strikes, according to regional governor Mario Smarkov and maritime security sources. The vessel was transporting 3,400 metric tons of liquefied petroleum gas from Egypt to Romania when it issued a distress signal. All 19 crew members were successfully rescued from the Black Sea.
articles.description: The Liberian-flagged Gas Husky was carrying 3,400 metric tons of LPG from Egypt to Romania when it sent a ‌distress signal

articles.headline: Odisha increases safety measures as cyclone Akvan shifts trajectory
articles.title: Odisha steps up preparedness as severe cyclone Akvan shifts towards coast
articles.summary: Severe cyclonic storm Akvan is expected to make landfall between Narsapur and Puri on November 20, prompting Odisha to evacuate residents from vulnerable areas. The India Meteorological Department forecasts heavy rainfall across several districts. Authorities have suspended beach tourism and recreational activities to protect the public as the weather system moves across the Bay.
articles.description: Officials said the strategy was being devised to cope with the calamity, mostly heavy rain in the State, as the IMD had forecast less than 100 kmph wind speed in the State even during the landfall period

articles.headline: Who is the terrorist security forces still tracking in Kulgam? | The Hindu Editorial
articles.title: Who is the terrorist security forces still tracking in Kulgam? | The Hindu Editorial
articles.description: A fresh encounter broke out in Jammu and Kashmir’s Kulgam district as security forces continued operations against terrorists linked to last week’s attack on a CRPF post. The renewed exchange of fire comes days after security forces killed Umar Nisar Dar, an accused in the attack that injured three CRPF personnel. Officials say the search is now focused on tracking down Mohammad Lateef Bhat, who allegedly escaped an earlier cordon during anti-terror operations in the district.

articles.headline: Andaman and Nicobar Islands implement new prison regulatory framework
articles.title: Andaman junks two colonial-era laws with new prison regulation
articles.summary: The Andaman and Nicobar Islands have replaced colonial-era laws with the Prisons and Correctional Services Regulation, 2026. The new framework mandates technology-driven security, including biometric identification and CCTV surveillance. It also establishes specific inmate classifications, prohibits caste-based discrimination, and introduces a grievance redressal mechanism to improve prison administration and oversight across the union territory.
articles.description: It will come into force on dates notified by the administrator, with different provisions allowed to take effect on different dates

articles.headline: Fresh encounter erupts in Kulgam as security forces hunt terrorists behind CRPF attack
articles.title: Fresh encounter erupts in Kulgam as security forces hunt terrorists behind CRPF attack
articles.description: A fresh encounter broke out in Jammu and Kashmir’s Kulgam district as security forces continued operations against terrorists linked to last week’s attack on a CRPF post. The renewed exchange of fire comes days after security forces killed Umar Nisar Dar, an accused in the attack that injured three CRPF personnel. Officials say the search is now focused on tracking down Mohammad Lateef Bhat, who allegedly escaped an earlier cordon during anti-terror operations in the district.

articles.headline: New York Times report on Iranian dams draws fierce criticism from experts
articles.title: Why has an NYT report on Iran’s dams ignited fierce pushback?
articles.summary: A New York Times report suggesting Iranian dams might support missile programmes sparked backlash from commentators and cited experts who warned the claims could justify attacks on civilian infrastructure. Iranian officials condemned the allegations as malicious propaganda, while the newspaper defended its reporting as an accurate representation of expert research.
articles.description: The NYT faces backlash over report suggesting a possible link between Iranian dams and underground missile facilities.

articles.headline: Sudan war trauma drives surge in substance addiction and drug manufacturing
articles.title: Traumas of Sudan war lead to wave of drug addiction
articles.summary: The ongoing conflict between the Sudanese armed forces and the Rapid Support Forces has displaced millions and triggered a severe addiction crisis. Charitable facilities like Khartoum's Qadreen Center report surging demand for psychological support. Meanwhile, officials note an alarming expansion of illicit drug manufacturing and trafficking networks across several vulnerable regions of the country.
articles.description: Anguish caused by conflict sees a growing number of young people turn to drugs.

articles.headline: Jharkhand anti-corruption bureau arrests six officials in land scam
articles.title: RIMS land scam: Jharkhand ACB arrests six government officials
articles.summary: The Jharkhand Anti-Corruption Bureau arrested six government officials on November 17, 2026, for their alleged involvement in the Rajendra Institute of Medical Sciences land scam. The detainees include a former Deputy Collector and several former sub-registrars. Investigators found evidence that the officials conspired to illegally register and mutate land belonging to the Ranchi-based medical institute.
articles.description: “The ACB, in its probe, found the involvement of government officials in the illegal registration and mutation of land belonging to RIMS Ranchi,” it said

articles.headline: Madhya Pradesh police officer faces inquiry over planted drug threats
articles.title: Police threaten couple with fake drug case; CM Yadav suspends all six officers involved
articles.summary: A police inspector in Madhya Pradesh's Seoni district was line-attached and an inquiry launched after closed-circuit television footage showed officers threatening to plant marijuana in a couple's bag during a hotel search. Chhindwara Range Deputy Inspector General Rajesh Kumar Singh stated that further action depends on the ongoing investigation into the alleged misconduct.
articles.description: A CCTV footage showed some police officers threatening a couple of putting marijuana in their bags to make a fake case during a search at a private hotel in Seoni, Madhya Pradesh

articles.headline: Australia imposes sanctions on Israeli individuals and organisations over West Bank expansion
articles.title: Australia sanctions Israeli settlers, organisations over West Bank expansion
articles.summary: On November 18, 2026, Australia sanctioned three Israeli individuals and four organisations, including settler leader Daniella Weiss and builder Eliav Libi, over illegal settlement expansion and violence in the West Bank. Foreign Minister Penny Wong stated the measures aim to protect the two-state solution. The restrictions prohibit Australians from trading with or supporting the targeted parties.
articles.description: The measures prohibit Australians ​and Australian businesses from trading ‌with, or providing support to, the sanctioned individuals and organisations

articles.headline: Osmo develops artificial intelligence smell model achieving human-level olfactory intelligence
articles.title: This smell startup says its AI nose is as good as a human’s
articles.summary: Artificial intelligence startup Osmo has created a foundational smell model that founder Alex Wiltschko claims matches human olfactory intelligence. Operating from New Jersey, the company uses chemical sensors and data labelers to analyze scent molecules, despite skepticism from smell scientist Avery Gilbert regarding its marketing and reliance on human panels.
articles.description: In a lab near Newark Airport in New Jersey, a team of around 30 experienced human sniffers are slowly working their way through every odor on Earth. Their careful notes—“nutty,” “peachy,” “marine”—are cross-referenced with a chemical analysis to create a rich set of training data for what AI startup Osmo calls the world’s first foundation…

articles.headline: India introduces one-time settlement scheme offering environmental compensation relief to groundwater users
articles.title: Centre offers up to 75% relief in environmental compensation to groundwater users
articles.summary: The Ministry of Jal Shakti notified the Ground Water Charges Scheme on November 12, offering industries and other unauthorized users thirty to seventy-five percent relief on environmental compensation. Managed by the Central Ground Water Authority, the one-year initiative aims to improve regulatory compliance across nineteen states and union territories.
articles.description: One-time settlement scheme offers 30-75% relief on groundwater environmental compensation to regulate, regularise, and settle disputes across projects in 19 States and Union Territories

articles.headline: Adyar Ananda Bhavan sells majority stake to Bodhi Tree Systems
articles.title: A2B sells majority stake to Bodhi Tree in $180-million deal
articles.summary: Food chain Adyar Ananda Bhavan secured one hundred eighty million dollars in investments from Bodhi Tree Systems, yielding a majority stake in a deal valuing the brand at approximately three hundred fifty million dollars. Vishnu Shankar confirmed funds will modernize factories in Chennai and Bengaluru, expanding the business into western India and Europe, building on a network of roughly 160 restaurants.
articles.description: The deal values A2B at $350 million, says a source

articles.headline: United States proposes stricter rules and longer hiring process for employment-based green cards
articles.title: U.S. proposes tougher rules for employment-based green cards, longer hiring process
articles.summary: The United States Department of Labour proposed stricter rules on November 17, 2026, to modernise the Programme Electronic Review Management immigrant visa process. The changes extend advertising periods from thirty to ninety days, prohibit tailoring jobs for foreign workers, and require employers to consider qualified American applicants, including recently laid-off workers.
articles.description: Proposed changes would extend advertising periods, curb tailoring of jobs to foreign workers, shift to online recruitment, and increase scrutiny of employers’ efforts to hire Americans before sponsoring visas

articles.headline: Security forces kill top Lashkar-e-Taiba commander Lateef Bhat in Kulgam encounter
articles.title: Who was Lateef Bhat, LeT militant killed in Kulgam encounter?
articles.summary: Security forces killed twenty-two-year-old Lashkar-e-Taiba commander Lateef Bhat during a gunfight in Zangalpora village on November 18. According to police, Bhat was involved in recent attacks against security personnel and non-local laborers, and refused surrender appeals after taking shelter inside a local mosque.
articles.description: Union Home Minister Amit Shah said in a post on X that Bhat was Lashkar-e-Taiba’s ‘last known active local terrorist’ in the area

articles.headline: Police arrest two suspects over triple murder in Assam town Duliajan
articles.title: Online gaming debt led to triple murder in Assam's Duliajan: Police
articles.summary: Dibrugarh Police arrested painter Raju Das and plumber Amir Das at Simaluguri railway station on November 17 in connection with the murder of three members of the Bhuyan family. Investigators stated the suspects conspired to commit robbery after Raju incurred four lakh rupees in online betting debt.
articles.description: The prime accused, Raju Das, had to repay his father ₹4 lakh borrowed for online betting and lost in it, and roped in his associate Amir Das, a plumber, with the two killing three Bhuyan family members with a hammer

articles.headline: Deutsche Bank leak reveals millions in transactions linked to Trump, Epstein and Russia
articles.title: What do Deutsche Bank leaks reveal about Trump, Epstein and Russia?
articles.summary: A leak of more than fifteen million internal records from Deutsche Bank published on Tuesday revealed millions in transactions linked to United States President Donald Trump, late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, and Russian networks. The documents highlight historical compliance failures, suspicious account monitoring, and internal warnings regarding high-risk clients before the bank tightened its controls.
articles.description: Deutsche Bank leaks expose ties to Trump, Epstein, and global elites amid scrutiny over past financial misconduct.

articles.headline: Ghanaian government defends purchase of new presidential jet amid public criticism
articles.title: Ghana's new $60m presidential jet sparks public outrage
articles.summary: The government of Ghana defended its acquisition of a $61m French-made Falcon 6X presidential jet delivered on Monday to the Ghana Air Force. Opposition politicians and citizens criticised the expenditure due to high living costs and past opposition by President John Mahama, but officials insisted the purchase is justified by improved economic stability and replaces an ageing, faulty aircraft.
articles.description: The purchase has sparked outrage over its cost as many Ghanaians struggle with rising cost of living.

articles.headline: India-UK ties outride Modi’s ‘decolonisation’ rhetoric
articles.title: India-UK ties outride Modi’s ‘decolonisation’ rhetoric
articles.description: Prince William's visit highlights growing partnership between New Delhi and London, despite their colonial history.

articles.headline: Myanmar-linked arsenic pollution prompts clean water scramble in Thailand
articles.title: Myanmar-linked arsenic pollution prompts clean water scramble in Thailand
articles.description: Thai authorities race to provide safe water to villagers after arsenic from Myanmar mines contaminates Mekong River.

articles.headline: Mahendra Singh Dhoni retires from Indian Premier League to assume mentor role
articles.title: MS Dhoni’s IPL playing career: Milestones and records of the CSK icon
