articles.summary: Mahendra Singh Dhoni concluded his playing career in the Indian Premier League on November 17, 2026, transitioning to a team mentor position for the Chennai Super Kings. The forty-five-year-old former Indian captain played seventeen seasons in the tournament, securing five titles and accumulating 5,439 runs. He will now join a revamped coaching staff ahead of the 2027 season alongside head coach Zaheer Khan.
articles.description: MS Dhoni, the CSK icon and one of Indian cricket’s most influential figures, announced his retirement from the IPL on November 17, 2026, ending a 17-season stint with Chennai Super Kings.

articles.headline: Paris Hilton and AOC speak against AI-generated deepfakes
articles.title: Paris Hilton and AOC speak against AI-generated deepfakes
articles.description: US Congresswoman AOC and TV personality Paris Hilton spoke against AI-generated deepfakes that target women and girls.

articles.headline: ‘We want to go back’: Rohingya refugees pin hopes on ICJ genocide verdict
articles.title: ‘We want to go back’: Rohingya refugees pin hopes on ICJ genocide verdict
articles.description: After almost a decade in exile, they're hoping the ICJ rules in their favour. But will that help them get back home?

articles.headline: Haitians rally in celebration of El Salvador’s anti-gang troop deployment
articles.title: Haitians rally in celebration of El Salvador’s anti-gang troop deployment
articles.description: Hundreds of Haitians have taken to the streets, celebrating El Salvador’s anti-gang military troops.

articles.headline: Security forces neutralise Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorist in Kulgam encounter
articles.title: Nation salutes brave jawans: Shah after LeT terrorist killed in J&K encounter
articles.summary: Indian security forces killed Lateef Bhat, identified as Lashkar-e-Taiba's last known active local terrorist in the Kashmir valley, during an operation in Kulgam district. Union Home Minister Amit Shah praised the coordination between the Jammu and Kashmir Police, Indian Army, Central Reserve Police Force, and intelligence agencies. The slain operative was wanted for a November 11 attack on a paramilitary post that injured three personnel.
articles.description: Security forces shot dead Lateef Bhat, who was wanted for the November 11 attack on a CRPF post

articles.headline: Pan American Health Organisation revokes United States measles elimination status
articles.title: Why did the U.S. lose its measles elimination status? | Explained
articles.summary: The United States lost its measles elimination status on November 17, 2026, after the Pan American Health Organisation recorded over 5400 infections. The United States Centers for Disease Control and Prevention stated that this represents the highest annual total since 1989 to 1991. According to Unicef data, 96 percent of patients were unvaccinated, with children under five years old accounting for 18 percent of cases.
articles.description: What triggered the resurgence of measles in the U.S.? Is vaccine hesitancy putting decades of progress against measles at risk? How is the global measles surge affecting India?

articles.headline: Enforcement Directorate moves Supreme Court against Azam Khan bail
articles.title: Supreme Court declines status quo against High Court allowing interim bail to Azam Khan
articles.summary: The Directorate of Enforcement has filed a Special Leave Petition in the Supreme Court to challenge the interim bail granted to Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan by the Allahabad High Court. Additional Solicitor General S.V. Raju mentioned the matter before a Bench led by Chief Justice Surya Kant on November 18, 2026, seeking an urgent hearing.
articles.description: Supreme Court agrees to hear ED appeal against bail on November 19

articles.headline: Forensic expert claims Jeffrey Epstein died of homicidal strangulation rather than suicide
articles.title: Epstein’s death more likely homicide than suicide, forensic expert says
articles.summary: Analysing autopsy records and photos, forensic expert Michael Freeman told CBS News that sex offender Jeffrey Epstein was likely murdered by strangulation from behind in his New York jail cell on August 10, 2019. Freeman stated the injuries were inconsistent with suicidal hanging, prompting his brother Mark Epstein to call for a new investigation, while the New York City Office of Chief Medical Examiner maintained its original ruling.
articles.description: An analysis of autopsy records and photos suggests the US sex offender was murdered in 2019, an expert says.

articles.headline: Magnitude 4.1 earthquake strikes Chamoli district in Uttarakhand
articles.title: Magnitude-4.1 earthquake hits Uttarakhand's Chamoli
articles.summary: An earthquake measuring 4.1 on the Richter scale struck the Chamoli district of Uttarakhand on November 18, 2026, according to officials. The tremors occurred at 10:21 a.m. with an epicentre near Jyotirmath at a depth of 10 km beneath the Earth, and the district administration reported no damage so far across the affected areas.
articles.description: No reports of damage so far; epicentre was near Jyotirmath in Chamoli district and tremors were felt across most parts of the district

articles.headline: Israeli Parliament elects Matan Kahana as new Knesset Speaker backed by Netanyahu opponents
articles.title: Israeli Parliament elects new Knesset Speaker backed by Netanyahu's opponents
articles.summary: The Israeli Parliament elected Matan Kahana as the new Knesset Speaker with 66 votes, replacing Amir Ohana. Backed by opposition parties and Gadi Eisenkot's bloc, the appointment grants the anti-Netanyahu coalition a legislative advantage to advance priorities including term limits for the prime minister and an inquiry into the October 7 attacks.
articles.description: The newly-elected Speaker is Matan Kahana, an ally of Gadi Eisenkot, the party leader currently working to form the next government and replace Mr. Netanyahu

articles.headline: Secretary of State Marco Rubio says no information links technical outages to malign actors.
articles.title: Marco Rubio says ‘zero’ information that U.S. outages are linked or caused by a malign actor
articles.summary: United States Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated on November 17, 2026, that there is no evidence connecting recent technological failures across the country to malicious actors or cyberattacks. The service disruptions affected Microsoft, JPMorgan Chase, air traffic control systems, and a National Security Agency network. While corporate and government entities attributed the issues to internal upgrades or software bugs, the repeated failures triggered widespread public skepticism and demands for government transparency.
articles.description: President Donald Trump faced a groundswell of criticism as friends and foes alike said the White House must answer for a cascade of service outages that snarled travel, cut off work, limited bank access and disrupted classified communications

articles.headline: CCMB scientists identify new strategy to prevent fungal infections from becoming invasive
articles.title: CCMB study points to new way of tackling fungal infections
articles.summary: Researchers at the CSIR-Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology in Hyderabad discovered small molecules targeting sugar metabolism that block Candida albicans from forming filament-like structures. Published in ACS Infectious Diseases, the study found the compounds keep the fungus in a harmless rounded form without killing it directly, improving survival rates in a mouse model and offering a potential alternative to traditional antifungal resistance.
articles.description: Fungi can gradually develop resistance to current antifungal drugs, making infections increasingly difficult to treat

articles.headline: Indian seafarer missing following vessel attack in Strait of Hormuz
articles.title: Indian national missing after attacks on commercial vessel in Strait of Hormuz
articles.summary: One Indian national is missing and two others were injured after their Panama-flagged LPG tanker MT Tara Gas came under attack in the Strait of Hormuz on November 16, 2026. According to the Ministry of External Affairs, 21 of the 24 Indian crew members were safely evacuated to Khasab. New Delhi condemned the incident, emphasizing that ongoing assaults on shipping lanes threaten seafarer safety and must cease immediately.
articles.description: MEA said that of the 24 Indian nationals on board MT Tara Gas, 21 have been safely evacuated

articles.headline: Delhi Police defend male officers handling women in crowd control
articles.title: No mandate only women personnel can ‘handle’ women in crowd-control operations, Delhi Police to SC
articles.summary: The Delhi Police informed the Supreme Court that deploying only female officers for crowd control is not a statutory mandate, responding to petitions regarding the manhandling of female protesters and journalists. In an affidavit, authorities stated that using male personnel depends on operational considerations, while adding that content creators are not legally classified as working journalists.
articles.description: The police said it was yet to be determined if “reel-makers can be elevated to the status of journalists or reporters”.

articles.headline: Congress-led UDF government in Keralam marks six months in office
articles.title: Six months of Keralam UDF govt: is the administration lumbering or hitting the ground running?
articles.summary: The Congress-led United Democratic Front government in Keralam marked six months in office on November 18, 2026, prompting debates on whether the administration has expedited its transformative vision for development and welfare or if it is still strolling as promised by Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan.
articles.description: As the government enters its sixth month in office on November 18, the question hovering over the polity is whether the ruling alliance’s actions have matched its soaring rhetoric about expediting a transformative vision for Keralam’s development and welfare

articles.headline: Ships risk Hormuz Strait due to limited US protection
articles.title: Ships risk Hormuz Strait due to limited US protection
articles.description: Elisabeth Braw with the Atlantic Council says US navy cannot protection to every vessel passing the Hormuz Strait.

articles.headline: Thomas Markle charged with child sexual abuse material in Philippines
articles.title: Philippines police ask prosecutors to charge Thomas Markle over child sex abuse material
articles.summary: Philippine police filed charges against Thomas Markle Senior on Monday for possessing and intending to distribute child sexual abuse material. Prosecutor Graeme Elmido confirmed the development following the discovery of seized devices from Markle's former residence. Currently held in the United States after a separate arrest by the Federal Bureau of Investigation, Markle has previously denied all allegations.
articles.description: Markle is being held in custody in the US after one charge and has previously denied all of the allegations.

articles.headline: Russian military transport plane crashes in western Siberia, killing nineteen people
articles.title: Russian military transport plane crashes in Siberia, killing 19: Defence Ministry
articles.summary: An Antonov-12 military transport aircraft crashed in western Siberia on November 17, 2026, resulting in the deaths of all nineteen people on board according to the Defence Ministry. The incident occurred in an unpopulated area near Kemerovo, with preliminary findings indicating equipment failure as the cause. Emergency responders extinguished a resulting fire near the village of Yagunovo while the Investigative Committee launched a formal inquiry.
articles.description: The An-12 aircraft went down in an unpopulated area near the city of Kemerovo, about 3,000 kilometres (about 1,860 miles) east of Moscow

articles.headline: UK transfers detained US soldier accused of Russia spying to America
articles.title: U.K. hands NATO-assigned American soldier accused of Russia spying to U.S.
articles.summary: British police transferred Lieutenant Colonel Brandon Tyner, a forty-one-year-old American soldier stationed with the North Atlantic Treaty Organization, into United States military custody following espionage allegations. Counter Terrorism Policing confirmed the handover occurred after an extensive investigation into suspected national security violations. The Kremlin denied any links to the detained officer.
articles.description: A U.S. Army official has named the detained soldier as 41-year-old Lieutenant Colonel Brandon Tyner

articles.headline: Jay Shah reappointed unopposed as International Cricket Council chairman
articles.title: Jay Shah reappointed unopposed as ICC Chairman for second term
articles.summary: The International Cricket Council announced on November 16, 2026, that thirty-eight-year-old Jay Shah was reappointed unopposed for a second two-year term. The decision was finalised during board meetings ending November 15, 2026, to provide leadership continuity as cricket prepares for its return to the Olympics at the 2028 Los Angeles Games.
articles.description: Jay Shah took over in December 2024 and was reappointed during the global body's Board Meetings that ended in Bali

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh deploys disaster response teams for Cyclone Akvan
articles.title: Andhra keeps 13 NDRF and 11 SDRF teams ready for Cyclone Akvan
articles.summary: Andhra Pradesh Home Minister Vangalapudi Anitha announced that 13 National Disaster Response Force teams and 11 State Disaster Response Force units are positioned for emergency relief operations regarding Cyclone Akvan. Officials reviewed preparedness on November 18, 2026, directing agencies to remain on high alert as heavy rainfall is anticipated across coastal districts.
articles.description: People can call 112, 1070 or 18004250101 in an emergency, and report power cuts, fallen trees and waterlogging on WhatsApp at 95523 00009

articles.headline: Maharashtra declares four additional talukas as drought-affected
articles.title: Maharashtra declares four more talukas drought-hit; total rises to 308
articles.summary: The Maharashtra government added Chiplun, Wada, Vikramgad, and Dindori to its drought list on November 17, 2026, raising the affected total to 308 out of 358 talukas. Revenue Minister Chandrashekhar Bawankule stated that 4,701.6 crore rupees have already been distributed to 94.3 lakh farmers across the state to mitigate ongoing water scarcity and crop losses.
articles.description: The four newly added talukas are Chiplun, Wada and Vikramgad in Konkan, and Dindori in Nashik district; ₹4,701.6 crore has been distributed to 94.3 lakh farmers across the State so far

articles.headline: BJP criticises Rahul Gandhi for remarks on Indian economy
articles.title: Leader of anti-India propaganda: BJP targets Rahul over his remarks at Columbia University
articles.summary: Bharatiya Janata Party leaders have strongly condemned Congress politician Rahul Gandhi following his recent speech at Columbia University in New York. According to the ruling party, his characterisation of India as an economic disaster contradicts positive data from global institutions such as the International Monetary Fund and Moody's, which project strong gross domestic product growth for the country.
articles.description: In a fireside chat at Columbia University in New York, Rahul Gandhi said India is sitting on an "economic disaster" with massive unemployment

articles.headline: Tribal healers in India establish conservation initiatives for medicinal plants
articles.title: The long walk to keep India’s tribal healing system alive
articles.summary: Traditional healers across several states are working to protect dwindling medicinal plant species threatened by climate change and human activities. During a convention organised by the Tata Steel Foundation in Jamshedpur, participants highlighted the scarcity of natural remedies. Meanwhile, health ministries are seeking to integrate tribal practitioners into public health outreach programs to improve regional disease monitoring and patient referrals.
articles.description: More than 200 tribal healers raised serious concerns over the disappearance of medicinal plants and its impact on their practice at Samvaad-2026, a five-day tribal convention organised by Tata Steel Foundation in Jamshedpur

articles.headline: South Asian cities face severe winter smog and high pollution levels
articles.title: What’s in the air you breathe? How to stay safe during smog season
articles.summary: Urban centers across the region are experiencing hazardous air quality as meteorological conditions trap pollutants near the ground during winter. Monitoring platforms recorded air quality index readings exceeding three hundred fifty in New Delhi, driven by vehicle exhaust, industrial emissions, and crop burning. International health organisations report that particulate matter poses significant risks to respiratory health, prompting various municipal authorities to implement targeted traffic and fuel restrictions.
articles.description: India and Pakistan had 42 of the world’s 50 most polluted cities in 2025. Millions now face another toxic winter.

articles.headline: Cricket Australia announces independent forum regarding 2018 ball-tampering scandal
articles.title: Cricket Australia announces independent forum in attempt to clear up Sandpapergate scandal
articles.summary: Cricket Australia plans to establish an independent forum to address conflicting accounts surrounding the two thousand eighteen Sandpapergate controversy in South Africa. Interim chair David Boon stated the initiative offers a respectful environment for past players and staff to share experiences without facing sanctions. Chief executive Todd Greenberg noted that the process aims to resolve lingering tensions following recent public comments from former athletes.
articles.description: CA’s interim chair David Boon says the ongoing controversy was a distraction for the sport, and hopes players and staffers on the 2018 test cricket team will take part in the forum

articles.headline: Rafael Grossi campaigns for United Nations secretary-general position
articles.title: Rafael Grossi is eyeing the UN’s top job. Will US support nuke his chances?
articles.summary: International Atomic Energy Agency chief Rafael Grossi is competing to succeed Antonio Guterres as United Nations secretary-general. The Argentinian nominee has advanced in Security Council straw polls but faces opposition from veto-wielding members like Russia and China over his alignment with Washington. Observers note his campaign focuses on institutional reform, though critics express concern regarding potential impacts on global governance.
articles.description: The nuclear watchdog chief is seen as technically competent, but questions remain about his plans for UN reform.

articles.headline: Four candidates challenge Gianni Infantino for the FIFA presidency
articles.title: FIFA election: Who are Infantino’s challengers, and will he be re-elected?
articles.summary: Four contenders are challenging incumbent Gianni Infantino in the upcoming Fédération Internationale de Football Association presidential election scheduled for March 18, 2027, in Rabat, Morocco. Infantino faces opposition from Philippe Diallo, Kozo Tashima, and Ramon Vega following a controversial attempt to sell World Cup commercial stakes. Legal experts also question his eligibility to serve a fourth term.
articles.description: A look at FIFA's presidential election process, the challengers and key dates, as Gianni Infantino seeks a fourth term.

articles.headline: Indian stock markets decline in early trade following recent gains
articles.title: Stock markets fall in early trade after two-day rally
articles.summary: Benchmark equity indices Sensex and Nifty declined in early trade on November 18, 2026, driven by profit-taking after a two-day rally. The 30-share BSE Sensex dropped 75.10 points to 82,482.30, while the NSE Nifty fell 26.95 points to 25,355.65. Major laggards included Tata Consultancy Services and Titan, whereas Maruti and ICICI Bank posted gains during the session.
articles.description: From the Sensex pack, Tata Consultancy Services, Titan, Asian Paints, Bajaj Finserv, Bajaj Finance, and Tata Steel were among the major laggards

articles.headline: Lobito Corridor railway aims to transport critical minerals and boost regional economic cooperation
articles.title: Can a US-backed mineral highway bring peace and prosperity to DR Congo?
articles.summary: The United States-backed Lobito Corridor project utilizes the Benguela Railway and the Port of Lobito to transport copper and cobalt from the Democratic Republic of Congo and Zambia to Western markets. Supported by over seven hundred fifty million dollars in funding, the route seeks to diversify mineral supplies, reduce reliance on China, and foster regional development.
articles.description: The Lobito Corridor is at the centre of a US-backed effort to secure access to Africa's critical minerals.

articles.headline: Historical examination revisits controversial underarm delivery by Trevor Chappell
articles.title: Sandpapergate and rubbing the wrong way
articles.summary: Australian cricket history reflects recurring debates surrounding sportsmanship, highlighted by Trevor Chappell delivering an underarm ball against New Zealand in 1981 at captain Greg Chappell's insistence. The controversial play, though legal at the time, prompted widespread outrage and led authorities to rewrite the Laws of the Game to explicitly ban underarm bowling. Greg Chappell later cited fixture exhaustion and tournament pressure as the primary reasons behind the tactical decision that impacted international cricket relations.
articles.description: Khawaja has set the cat amongst the pigeons and the repercussions, if any, of his expose in the scandal will manifest themselves in the next few weeks and months, when Australia are confronted with a packed schedule

articles.headline: Nepal receives Indian approval to import electricity during winter
articles.title: Nepal gets nod to import 350 MW of power from India during winter
articles.summary: Nepal has obtained authorization to import up to 350 megawatts of electricity from India from November 17, 2026, to July 31, 2027. According to Nepal Electricity Authority Managing Director Dirghayu Kumar Shrestha, the supply will help offset domestic generation shortfalls caused by seasonal water level drops and flood damage to several hydropower facilities.
articles.description: The approval is valid from November 17, 2026, to July 31, 2027, and is expected to help Nepal manage the seasonal gap between electricity demand and domestic generation

articles.headline: Voyager 1 reaches a distance of one light-day from the earth
articles.title: Voyager 1, one light-day away from earth today, is a marvel of science
articles.summary: The Voyager 1 spacecraft has reached a milestone by traveling nearly 26 billion kilometres away from the earth. According to reports published on November 18, 2026, communication signals now take a full day to travel each way between the probe and receivers on the ground. Operating since February 17, 1998, as the most distant space mission, the craft continues traveling at 61,000 kilometres per hour while remaining within the broader gravitational and magnetic influence of the solar system.
articles.description: Measurements lying in the shadows of their successors can find new lives in the light of new theories. The Voyager 1 mission’s longevity made that more apparent, allowing successive generations of researchers to find more uses for its data even as it continues to collect new information

articles.headline: Marco Rubio dismisses systemic attack concerns following recent technology outages
articles.title: Rubio says US not 'under systemic attack' after series of tech outages
articles.summary: United States Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated there is zero evidence connecting recent technology disruptions across banking, aviation, and major tech firms like Microsoft and Apple. Cybersecurity experts and officials, including United States Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton, attributed the incidents to aging infrastructure and system upgrades rather than hostile cyber activity.
articles.description: Secretary of State Marco Rubio said there was "zero evidence" supporting theories online that recent disruptions affecting Microsoft, banks and flights are connected.

articles.headline: Bhagyalakshmi temple near Charminar expands and draws massive crowds for Deepavali
articles.title: The expansion of Bhagyalakshmi Temple near Hyderabad’s Charminar | Explained
articles.summary: The Bhagyalakshmi Temple near the Charminar in Hyderabad has expanded to cover much of the south-eastern flank of the nationally protected monument. According to police officials, about five lakh visitors reached the site during Deepavali on November 8 to receive free silver-stamped tokens, which devotees later noted appeared to be made of aluminium, causing massive traffic congestion.
articles.description: One of the first letters the ASI wrote to the Commission of Municipal Corporation of Hyderabad was on December 13, 1968, alerting the civic body of the construction

articles.headline: ICMR-NIN study reveals thiamine deficiency among women in Northeast India
articles.title: One in five women in parts of Northeast deficient in vitamin B1: ICMR-NIN study
articles.summary: Around one in five pregnant and lactating women in Assam's Barak Valley and adjoining Tripura suffer from suboptimal thiamine levels, according to a community-based study by the ICMR-National Institute of Nutrition in Hyderabad. Published in the Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences, researchers found that rice-based diets and specific dietary practices contributed to the deficiency risk.
articles.description: Vitamin B1 or Thiamine is an essential micronutrient that supports energy metabolism and healthy nervous system function

articles.headline: Nearly 75 lakh names added in draft SSR voters lists across states
articles.title: Nearly 75 lakh names added in draft SSR voters lists in 13 States and UTs
articles.summary: Nearly 75 million more names have been added in draft voter lists published in 13 States and Union Territories via a special summary revision process. Uttar Pradesh added 18.84 lakh names, while Goa saw the highest rate at 3.01%. Unlike the special intensive revision, voters do not need citizenship documents for SSR enrolment, and the Election Commission of India directed that machine-readable PDFs be provided to candidates.
articles.description: These States/UTs saw their combined electorate shrink from 49.6 cr to 45.2 cr post-SIR, but SSR has resulted in a recovery to almost 46 cr in draft SSR list; U.P. has highest number of voters added through SSR, but Goa sees highest growth in percentage terms

articles.headline: Rubio rules out cyberattacks or links between tech outages
articles.title: Rubio rules out cyberattacks or links between tech outages
articles.description: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said there is no evidence linking technical outages to each other or to cyberattacks.

articles.headline: Demand for air purifiers surges across Delhi-NCR amid worsening air pollution
articles.title: Delhi’s air pollution: What can an air purifier really do? | Explained
articles.summary: Demand for air purifiers has surged across Delhi-NCR and adjoining parts of north India following Diwali as residents face worsening air pollution. E-commerce platforms reported products going out of stock, with devices priced between ₹3,500 and ₹56,900, though consumers often lack clarity on what these devices can actually filter to protect health.
articles.description: With sales surging amid worsening air quality across Delhi-NCR, pulmonologists explain what air purifiers can filter, what they cannot remove and how much protection they offer against pollution

articles.headline: Waymo temporarily suspends driverless vehicle operations on all United States freeways
articles.title: Waymo pulls driverless taxis from all US freeways
articles.summary: Alphabet-owned autonomous vehicle company Waymo has temporarily halted driverless vehicle operations across all United States freeways following an enforcement action by the California Department of Motor Vehicles. The state ban was enacted after driverless taxis repeatedly entered active construction zones on November 11. Although highway testing remains restricted, the company's vehicles continue to provide rides on regular municipal streets across fifteen cities.
articles.description: The decision comes after California banned Waymo's driverless vehicles from operating on the state's highways following a series of traffic incidents.

articles.headline: Kulgam security operations continue as officials find deceased accomplice of Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorist.
articles.title: Kulgam anti-terror ops. continue; body of LeT terrorist Lateef Bhat’s ‘accomplice’ retrieved from encounter site
articles.summary: Security forces in South Kashmir's Kulgam maintained stringent anti-terror operations on November 17, 2026, retrieving the body of Umar Nisar Dar, an alleged accomplice of Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorist Lateef Bhat. The prolonged lockdown in civilian areas drew sharp criticism from regional political leaders, including National Conference spokesman Imran Nabi Dar and Peoples Democratic Party president Mehbooba Mufti, who condemned the collective punishment imposed on local residents.
articles.description: Security agencies released CCTV footage, which suggested Dar and Bhat were seen together on November 10 and 11 surveying multiple locations

articles.headline: Rare images of uncontacted Amazon Indigenous group highlight threats from illegal intruders.
articles.title: Rare images of Indigenous group in Amazon highlight threats, advocates say
articles.summary: Survival International released rare footage on November 17, 2026, showing an isolated group of Awa people interacting with villagers in Maranhao, Brazil. Indigenous advocates and agencies warn that the historic encounter underscores extreme territorial pressures from illegal loggers and ranchers. Experts emphasize that such unplanned contacts pose severe health risks, potentially exposing vulnerable populations to fatal diseases without immediate protection.
articles.description: Illegal activities in the Amazon pose grave risks to uncontacted Indigenous groups like Brazil’s Awa,.

articles.title: ICE agents shove and pepper-spray pregnant woman
articles.description: An American woman was shoved to the ground and pepper-sprayed by ICE agents despite telling them she was pregnant.

articles.headline: United States President Donald Trump attends APEC summit to meet Chinese and Russian leaders.
articles.title: What is Trump hoping to achieve at APEC meeting in China?
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump arrived in Shenzhen, China, for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit to hold talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin. The diplomatic engagements follow recent Democratic victories in Congress and center on bilateral relations, trade, and artificial intelligence regulation. Observers expect the discussions to maintain strategic stability without producing major policy breakthroughs regarding ongoing trade or technology disputes.
articles.description: US president expected to meet with Chinese leader for third time this year; hold trilateral summit with Putin.

articles.headline: Bharatiya Janata Party accuses Congress of double standards over electoral roll revision
articles.title: Congress approves of SIR in Andamans and South but opposes it elsewhere: BJP
articles.summary: The Bharatiya Janata Party criticized the Congress party on November 17 for supporting the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands and southern states while opposing it in northern regions. articles.description: Kerala Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan described SIR as good, while Karnataka Minister Satish Jarkiholi called it constitutional. Why then is Rahul Gandhi opposing it, asked Gaurav Bhatia

articles.headline: Rahul Gandhi defends controversial parents remark by invoking Hindu temple sculpture
articles.title: Rahul Gandhi invokes Hindu faith to defend his ‘Mama sitting on Papa’s lap’ remark
articles.summary: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi defended his recent comments about his parents during an event on November 17, 2026, by referencing a temple sculpture depicting Hindu deities Shiva and Parvati. Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma and other Bharatiya Janata Party leaders previously criticized the remarks. The Congress party supported Gandhi, stating the discussion highlighted equality and affection in relationships.
articles.description: Responding to the BJP’s criticism of his remarks, Mr. Gandhi shares artwork depicting Goddess Parvati perched on Lord Shiva’s lap; says “love need not be hidden, affection is not a weakness, and equality begins with treating your partner as an equal.”

articles.headline: Nvidia chairperson says board does not intend to reinstate former chief executive Jensen Huang.

articles.summary: Nvidia Chairperson Harvey Jones announced on November 17, 2026, that the board of directors will not reinstate former chief executive Jensen Huang following his resignation over an extramarital affair. Despite leadership turmoil, Nvidia reported robust third-quarter financial results with over 116 billion dollars in revenue. Meanwhile, Huang agreed to voluntarily testify before United States House committees on December 1 regarding national security scrutiny and export control compliance.
articles.description: Jensen Huang acknowledged making "serious mistakes" in his personal life; In its third-quarter earnings statement released on November 17, Nvidia did not mention his ouster or possible return

articles.headline: Ecuadorian fishermen sue Trump administration over lethal drone strike
articles.title: Ecuadorian fishermen sue Trump administration over drone strike
articles.summary: Ecuadorian fishermen filed a lawsuit in a Pennsylvania federal court against the administration of United States President Donald Trump regarding a March drone strike that sank their vessel, La Negra Francisca Duarte II, and injured two crew members. The complaint seeks financial restitution and an end to strikes targeting alleged drug boats. The government has not claimed responsibility for the incident, which plaintiffs called part of an unlawful military campaign.
articles.description: Crew say their boat was attacked by drones launched from US-operated vessel as part of 'manifestly unlawful' campaign.

articles.headline: Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister mandates local hiring by outside companies

articles.summary: Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah stated on November 17, 2026, that external companies must hire local youths rather than outsiders. Speaking during a project inauguration in Jammu, Samba, and Kathua districts, Mr. Abdullah criticized the excuse of lacking trained personnel, noting that institutions like Industrial Training Institutes can prepare regional workers. He also addressed the region's Union Territory status.
articles.description: He made the statement during the inauguration of development projects worth ₹30 crores in Jammu, Samba and Kathua districts

articles.headline: Diplomatic efforts fail to halt escalating violence in eastern DRC
articles.title: DR Congo’s rival peace efforts fail to halt violence in the east

The Front for recent advances through Kahuzi-Biega National Park prompted the Congolese army to prepare counteroffensives. Meanwhile, humanitarian organizations like Doctors Without Borders reduced staff presence in vulnerable zones as displaced communities face mounting security risks and disrupted services.
articles.description: Diplomatic efforts struggle to end fighting in eastern DRC as civilians continue to bear the cost of conflict.

articles.title: Israel parliament elects Gadi Eisenkot ally Matan Kahana as new speaker
articles.summary: Lawmakers in Israel elected Matan Kahana as parliament speaker on Tuesday after receiving sixty-six votes in the legislative chamber. Kahana, an ally of party leader Gadi Eisenkot, defeated Likud candidate Ofir Katz. The appointment allows the opposition to potentially challenge outgoing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's domestic agenda and judicial reforms following recent inconclusive parliamentary elections.
articles.description: Eisenkot’s bloc has pledged to undo some of Netanyahu’s most contentious domestic policies following Kahana’s election.

articles.headline: Haitians protest in support of El Salvador military deployment
articles.title: Haitians protest in support of El Salvador’s anti-gang troop deployment
articles.summary: Demonstrators marched across multiple Haitian cities on Tuesday to back the deployment of troops from El Salvador. The military intervention followed the kidnapping of four Salvadoran aviation technicians near Port-au-Prince. Although El Salvador confirmed plans to withdraw its forces once the missing airmen are located, Haitian Justice Minister Patrick Pelissier expressed strong gratitude for the security assistance.
articles.description: El Salvador's security minister has confirmed the troops will leave once kidnapped technicians are rescued.

articles.headline: US Army officer arrested for suspected espionage is transferred to military custody
articles.title: American soldier arrested by UK police on suspicion of spying taken into US military custody
articles.summary: Lieutenant Colonel Brandon Carroll Tyner, a forty-one-year-old US Army officer arrested in the United Kingdom on suspicion of spying for Russia, was transferred to United States military custody. British counter-terrorism police arrested the serviceman last week near Gloucester, where he was based at Imjin Barracks. Assistant Commissioner Laurence Taylor confirmed the investigation was handed over to American partners, while the Kremlin denied involvement.

articles.title: Russian military plane crash in Siberia kills 19
articles.summary: Nineteen people died when an Antonov An-12 transport aircraft crashed near Kemerovo in western Siberia, according to the Russian Defence Ministry. Investigators suspect equipment failure caused the accident in the unpopulated area. Regional Governor Ilya Seredyuk confirmed emergency crews extinguished a fire at the site near Yagunovo, while criminal authorities launched a formal safety inquiry.
articles.description: Russia's Defence Ministry says preliminary findings for the crash point to equipment failure.

articles.headline: UK police hand over US soldier accused of espionage to military
articles.title: UK hands NATO-assigned US soldier accused of Russia spying to US military

Federal Bureau of Investigation Director Kash Patel confirmed the service member remains held following a joint espionage probe.

The governing party, led historically by Nelson Mandela, swept to power thirty-two years ago following the end of apartheid. Analysts and party members discussed the severity of this political crisis and its implications for the nation on a program hosted by presenter James Bays.
articles.description: African National Congress won its lowest-ever vote share in local elections this month.

articles.headline: Prediction market Kalshi halts presidential speech wagers following regulatory order
articles.title: Kalshi halts Trump speech bets after CFTC order

The regulatory action follows insider trading concerns involving a White House teleprompter operator who traded on these markets. Consequently, the operator received a three-year ban and financial penalties, while regulatory scrutiny of prediction platforms has intensified.
articles.description: Kalshi halts Trump speech bets following CFTC mandate amid concerns of insider trading in US prediction markets.

Led by party president Nitin Nabin and Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, the party aims to showcase government achievements and strengthen booth-level management. articles.summary: United States House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries confirmed plans to force a recorded vote on his speaker nomination during upcoming Democratic leadership elections. The shift aims to counter progressive dissent and requires House Democrats to publicly state their support. Jeffries is expected to secure the nomination ahead of the 120th Congress being sworn in on January 3.
articles.description: The lawmaker is opting to put progressive opponents on record as he vies to become the chamber's first Black speaker.

articles.headline: Bangladesh connects first nuclear power plant at Rooppur to grid
